basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Major est iniquitas mea quam ut veniam merear. Ecce ejicis me hodie a facie tua, et a'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Major est iniquitas mea quam ut veniam merear. Ecce ejicis me hodie a facie tua, et a facie terrae abscondar, et ero vagus et profugus in terra. Ejicior, inquit, a conspectu tuo, et conscientia sceleris lucem ipsam ferre non sustinens, abscondar ut latitem. Vel certe ejicis me a facie terrae, ne videlicet in ulla terrarum regione, ne inter ullos habitatores ejus orbis securus liberque manere permittar, a facie quoque tua abscondar, ne hanc ultra videre merear, quam usque hodie saepius intuendo, ac tuam vocem audiendo, felicior vivebam.
